key_insight: Nominally cubic CsGeBr3 hosts long-lived, one-dimensional polar chains despite having zero net polarization, while its ferroelectric phase switches polarization chain by chain.
engineering_relevance: Slow local polarization dynamics could inform halide-perovskite device models, but the abstract does not establish effects on solar-cell performance.
method: Comparison with BaTiO3, PbTiO3, and CsSnBr3
evidence_signal: Simulations show polar chains extending at least tens of nanometers and relaxing on nanosecond timescales, four orders of magnitude slower than in BaTiO3 and PbTiO3.
watch_item: Experimental validation and relevance to operating solar cells remain unestablished in the abstract.
paper_title: Anomalous polar chains in halide perovskites
